Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinHeap and HeapSort Implementation in JavaScript

Main goal of the code:
- Implements a min-heap data structure and uses it to perform heap-based sorting (heap sort) on an iterable.

What the code does:
- MinHeap class:
  - Stores elements in an array this.heap to represent a binary min-heap.
  - push(value): inserts a value and restores heap order via _siftUp.
  - pop(): removes and returns the smallest element (root). Replaces root with last element and restores heap order via _siftDown. Returns undefined if the heap is empty.
  - size(): returns the number of elements in the heap.
  - _siftUp(): moves the newly added element up the heap until the parent is smaller or equal.
  - _siftDown(): moves the root element down to maintain the min-heap property by selecting the smaller child to swap with.

- heapSort(iterable):
  - Creates a MinHeap, pushes all values from the input iterable into it.
  - Repeatedly pops the minimum element from the heap to build a new sorted array.
  - Returns the sorted array (in ascending order).

In short, the code provides a min-heap with push/pop operations and a function to sort an iterable by repeatedly extracting the minimum value from the heap.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Min-Heap Based Generation of nth Super Ugly Number

Main goal: Compute the nth super ugly number given a list of prime factors, using a custom min-heap to generate numbers in increasing order without duplicates.

What the code does:
- MinHeap class:
  - Implements a binary min-heap that stores objects with a numeric val and supports push and pop.
  - push(item): adds an item and reorders up to maintain heap property.
  - pop(): removes and returns the smallest item (root), replacing it with the last element and reordering down.
  - _heapifyUp/_heapifyDown: maintain the heap invariant by comparing items based on their val field.
- nthSuperUglyNumber(n, primes):
  - Generates the nth super ugly number, where a super ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are all in the given primes array.
  - Initializes uglies with [1].
  - Creates a MinHeap containing initial candidates for each prime: { val: prime, prime: prime, idx: 0 }.
  - Repeatedly pops the smallest candidate from the heap:
    - If the popped value is not a duplicate of the last produced ugly number, appends it to uglies.
    - Pushes a new candidate for the same prime: val = prime * uglies[node.idx + 1], with updated idx + 1.
  - Stops when uglies length reaches n and returns the last element (the nth super ugly number).

Notes:
- Uses a deduplication check by comparing with the last element in uglies to avoid duplicates in the sequence.
- The heap stores objects and orders them by the val property to function as a priority queue of candidate multiples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Common Subsequence of Three Strings (3D DP)

Main goal of the code:
- This function computes the length of the longest common subsequence among three strings X, Y, and Z using a dynamic programming approach in three dimensions.

Key points:
- It builds a 3D DP table L with dimensions (m+1) x (n+1) x (o+1), where m, n, o are the lengths of X, Y, Z respectively.
- Base case: If any index is 0, the corresponding L[i][j][k] is 0 (subsequence with an empty string has length 0).
- If the current characters match (X[i-1] === Y[j-1] === Z[k-1]), it extends the common subsequence: L[i][j][k] = L[i-1][j-1][k-1] + 1.
- If they don’t all match, it takes the maximum subsequence length found by reducing one index at a time: max(L[i-1][j][k], L[i][j-1][k], L[i][j][k-1]).
- The function returns L[m][n][o], the length of the longest common subsequence among the three input strings.

mbpp_0423.reference_description: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Gold Collection in a Grid

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the maximum amount of gold that can be collected starting from any row in the first column and moving to the right, with allowed moves to the cell to the right, right-up, or right-down at each step, across an m x n grid of gold values.

What the functions do:
- getMaxGold(gold, m, n):
  - goldTable is a dynamic programming table (m x n) initialized with zeros.
  - Fills goldTable from right to left (columns from n-1 down to 0) and top to bottom (rows 0 to m-1).
  - For each cell (row, col), computes the best possible sum starting from that cell if you move only to the right, right-up, or right-down in subsequent columns:
    - right: value in the same row, next column (or 0 if at the last column)
    - rightUp: value from the cell diagonally up-right (or 0 if at top row or last column)
    - rightDown: value from the cell diagonally down-right (or 0 if at bottom row or last column)
  - goldTable[row][col] = gold[row][col] + max(right, rightUp, rightDown)
  - After filling, finds the maximum value in the first column (goldTable[i][0] for i in 0..m-1), which represents the best starting row in the first column.
  - Returns that maximum value as the result.

Title: Smallest Common Multiple Calculator with Restricted Factor Set

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the smallest positive multiple of n that is divisible by a specific set of numbers derived from n.

How it works (high level):
- For n > 2, it builds a list of “factors” consisting of numbers from n down to 2 for which number * 2 > n (i.e., numbers greater than n/2).
- It then iterates by incrementing i in steps of n (i starts at 2n) and checks whether i is divisible by every element in that factors list.
- If i is divisible by all elements in factors, it returns i as the result; otherwise it increases i by n and repeats.
- For n <= 2, it simply returns n.

In short: it finds the smallest multiple of n that is divisible by all integers greater than n/2 and up to n.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic programming calculation of a specific counting sequence

Main goal: The function getTotalNumberOfSequences(m, n) computes a value T[m][n] using a dynamic programming table, where:

- T is a (m+1) x (n+1) 2D array initialized to zero.
- For each i from 0..m and j from 0..n:
  - If i == 0 or j == 0: T[i][j] = 0.
  - If i < j: T[i][j] = 0.
  - If j == 1: T[i][j] = i.
  - Otherwise: T[i][j] = T[i - 1][j] + T[Math.floor(i / 2)][j - 1].

The function returns the value T[m][n], effectively counting or accumulating a quantity based on previous states, combining a state that decreases i by 1 with a state that halves i (rounded down) and decreases j by 1.

Main goal of the code:

What the functions do:
- findPeakUtil(arr, low, high, n):
  - Recursively searches for a peak between indices low and high.
  - Computes mid. If arr[mid] is a peak (greater than or equal to its neighbors, with boundary checks at the ends), returns mid.
  - If the left neighbor is greater than arr[mid], recursively searches the left half (low to mid-1).
  - Otherwise, recursively searches the right half (mid+1 to high).
- findPeak(arr, n):
  - Entry point that starts the search over the entire array (0 to n-1) by calling findPeakUtil.
- The function assumes a 0-based index array and returns the index of a peak element.

- avg_calc(ls): Calculates the average (mean) of the elements in ls. If the list has 1 or fewer elements, returns that single value.
- sd_calc(data): Computes the sample standard deviation of data. For 1 or fewer elements, returns 0. It uses avg_calc to obtain the mean, then applies the standard formula with Bessel's correction (divide by n-1).

mbpp_0714.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Prime Factorization Step Counter

Main goal of the code:
- The function countFac(n) processes the integer n to count a specific metric based on its prime factorization. For each prime factor i, it computes how many times i divides n (the exponent total). It then adds to a running count a series of values corresponding to the triangular numbers up to that exponent (effectively counting the number of terms in a sequence 1+2+...+total). After processing all factors up to sqrt(m), if a remaining factor n > 1 exists, it increments the count by 1. The function returns the final count.

mbpp_0181.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Common Prefix Finder for String Arrays

Main goal: The code computes the longest common prefix among the first n strings in an array by iteratively comparing each element with the current prefix and shrinking it using a pairwise comparison helper.

Functions:
- commonPrefixUtil(str1, str2): Returns the longest common prefix shared by two strings by scanning from the start until a mismatch occurs.
- commonPrefix(arr, n): Starts with the first string as the initial prefix and iteratively updates it by computing the common prefix with each subsequent array element up to index n-1, returning the final shared prefix.

mbpp_0853.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find sum of odd factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find sum of odd factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Compute the product of sums of odd factors of a number

Summary_description:
This function computes the sum of all odd divisors of a given positive integer n. It first removes all factors of 2, effectively focusing on the odd part. It then iterates over odd prime candidates starting from 3 up to sqrt(n), accumulating, for each prime factor i, the sum of all powers of i (1 + i + i^2 + ...). The result is the product of these sums for all odd prime factors. If a remaining n > 1 after the loop, it multiplies by (1 + n) to account for a final prime factor. The overall result is the sum of all odd divisors of the original input n.

mbpp_0386.reference_description: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Swap Count Between Brackets

Main goal of the code:
- The function swapCount(s) computes the number of adjacent swaps needed to balance a string of brackets consisting of '[' and ']'. It tracks imbalance (unmatched right brackets against left brackets) and accumulates the total swaps required to move brackets to achieve balance as it scans the string from left to right. The function returns the total swap count.

mbpp_0516.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Radix Sort Implementation in JavaScript

Main goal: To sort an array of non-negative integers in ascending order using the radix sort algorithm, processing digits from least significant to most significant and grouping numbers into buckets by each digit.

mbpp_0846.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Platform Allocation Problem – Minimum Number of Platforms Needed

Main goal of the code:
- Given arrival times (arr) and departure times (dep) of trains, the function computes the minimum number of platforms required so that no train has to wait. It does this by sorting both arrays and simulating the timeline, tracking how many platforms are currently in use and updating the maximum needed.

How it works (functions):
- sort both arr and dep in ascending order.
- Initialize platNeeded and result to 1, and two indices i (for arrivals) and j (for departures).
- Iterate while i and j are within bounds:
  - If the next arrival occurs before or at the same time as the next departure (arr[i] <= dep[j]), a new platform is needed (platNeeded++), advance i.
  - Otherwise, a platform becomes free (platNeeded--), advance j.
  - Update result if the current platNeeded exceeds the best (maximum) so far.
- Return result, the maximum number of platforms required at any time.

mbpp_0122.reference_description: Write a function to find n’th smart number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n’th smart number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Purpose and behavior of smartNumber function

Main goal: The code builds a list of numbers up to 3000 that are multiples of primes (specifically numbers j where primes[j] becomes -1 at some point via marking) and, after processing, sorts that list and returns the (n-1)th element. In essence, it attempts to collect certain composite numbers associated with prime indices, then returns the nth smallest such number.

mbpp_0032.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the largest prime factor of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the largest prime factor of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Finding the largest prime factor of a number

Main goal: The function maxPrimeFactors(n) computes and returns the largest prime factor of the given integer n. It repeatedly divides out factor 2, then iterates through odd potential factors up to the square root of the current n, updating the maximum prime factor found. If the remaining n is greater than 2, that n is itself the largest prime factor. The function returns the largest prime factor as an integer.

mbpp_0020.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: IsWoodall Function – Determines Woodall Numbers

Main goal of the code:
- The function isWoodall(x) checks whether a given integer x is a Woodall number.

What the code does:
- If x is even, it immediately returns false.
- If x equals 1, it returns true.
- It initializes m = x + 1 and a counter p = 0.
- It repeatedly divides m by 2 while m is even, incrementing p each time.
- If at any point p equals the current value of m, it returns true.
- If the loop ends without p ever equaling m, it returns false.

Summary:
- The function identifies Woodall numbers by testing whether, for x odd, repeatedly halving (x+1) yields a state where the number of halvings equals the current value of the halved number. If such a condition occurs, it returns true; otherwise, false.

mbpp_0395.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Non-Repeating Character Finder

Main goal of the code:
- Finds and returns the first character in a string that occurs exactly once.
- It preserves the order of first appearance using charOrder and a frequency map ctr.
- If no non-repeating character exists, it returns null.

mbpp_0856.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find minimum adjacent swaps required to sort binary array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find minimum adjacent swaps required to sort binary array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find Minimum Swaps to Bring Ones Together in a Binary Array

Summary_description: This function computes the minimum number of swaps required to move all 1s to the left (or end) of a binary array of length n. It builds a suffix array of zeros (noOfZeroes) indicating how many zeros remain from each position to the end, then sums, for every 1 encountered, the number of zeros to its right (the minimum swaps needed to relocate that 1 past those zeros). The result is the total minimum swaps needed to group all 1s together.

mbpp_0684.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count occurences of a character in a repeated string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to count occurences of a character in a repeated string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: The function countChar counts occurrences of a given character x in a string str, scaled to a fixed total length n = 10 by repeating the string as needed.

What it does:
- Counts how many times x appears in the entire str (initial count).
- Calculates how many full copies of str fit into a total length n (repetitions = floor(n / str.length)) and multiplies the initial count by that factor to estimate occurrences across the repeated copies.
- Handles the partial copy for the remaining characters (l = n % str.length) by scanning the first l characters of str and incrementing count when they equal x.
- Returns the final adjusted count.

Essentially, it estimates the total number of occurrences of x in a string formed by repeating str to reach a total length n (10), using both full copies and a partial tail.

mbpp_0492.reference_description: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Implement a binary search to determine whether a given item exists within a sorted array.

What it does:
- Takes a sorted list (itemList) and a target item.
- Uses a classic binary search: maintains search bounds (first, last), repeatedly checks the middle element.
- If a match is found, sets found to true and stops; otherwise narrows the search range by comparing the target with the middle element.
- Returns a boolean indicating whether the item is present in the list.

mbpp_0001.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming solution to minimum-cost path in a grid

Main goal of the code: Compute the minimum cost to travel from the top-left corner (0,0) to the bottom-right corner (m,n) of a 2D grid, where each cell has a cost Cost[i][j], and at each step you can move to the right, down, or diagonally down-right. The function builds a DP table of subproblem costs and returns the minimum total cost to reach (m,n).

mbpp_0231.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: JavaScript Function to Compute Maximum Path Sum in a Triangle

Summary_description:
This function modifies a given triangular array in place to compute the maximum total from the top to the bottom of the triangle. It uses dynamic programming to accumulate the largest possible sums at each position as it traverses rows. Specifically, it:
- Initializes the first row and, if applicable, the second row by adding the top element to the adjacent elements.
- Iterates through subsequent rows, updating edge elements by adding the value from the previous row's corresponding edge.
- For inner elements, it selects the larger of two possible previous-path sums (from the top-left or top) and adds the current value.
- Finally, it returns the maximum value found in the last row, representing the maximum path sum from top to bottom.

mbpp_0351.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Element Occurring Exactly k Times in Array

Main goal of the code:
- Given an array arr of length n and an integer k, the function first counts the frequency of each element in arr.
- It then scans the array from the start and returns the first element whose frequency equals k.
- If no element occurs exactly k times, it returns -1.

Key behavior:
- Uses a frequency map (countMap) to store counts.
- Returns the earliest element (by original order) with exactly k occurrences; otherwise -1.

mbpp_0283.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether the frequency of each digit is less than or equal to the digit itself.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to check whether the frequency of each digit is less than or equal to the digit itself.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Code Analysis – Digit Frequency Validation

Main goal: The function validate(n) checks whether, for every digit i from 0 to 9, the count of occurrences of digit i in n never exceeds i. If any digit appears more times than its value, the function returns false; otherwise it returns true after checking all digits.

mbpp_0071.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Comb Sort Implementation in JavaScript

Main goal: Sort an array of numbers in ascending order using the comb sort algorithm by repeatedly reducing the gap size and swapping out-of-order elements as needed.

Summary_description:
Implements comb sort by initializing a gap equal to the array length, shrinking the gap by a factor of 1.3 each pass, and performing pairwise comparisons/swaps for elements separated by the current gap until a full pass occurs with no swaps and the gap has reduced to 1. Returns the sorted array.

mbpp_0374.reference_description: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Permute a string by inserting first character into all positions of permutations of the rest

Main goal: Generate all unique permutations of a given string by recursively permuting the substring (excluding the first character) and then inserting the first character into every possible position of each of those permutations, collecting unique results.

mbpp_0506.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Permutation Coefficient Calculator

Main goal: Compute the number of permutations of n items taken k at a time with repetition allowed (the k-th partial Stirling-like coefficient) by dynamic programming. The function builds a 2D table P where P[i][j] accumulates the count, using the recurrence P[i][j] = P[i-1][j] + j * P[i-1][j-1], with base case P[i][0] = 1, and returns P[n][k].

mbpp_0415.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Max Product Pair Finder

Main goal of the code:
- To find two elements in an array whose product is the maximum among all pairs, and return that pair as [x, y]. If the array has fewer than two elements, it returns "No pairs exists". It uses a brute-force double loop to compare products of all unique pairs and tracks the pair with the largest product.

mbpp_0428.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using shell sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using shell sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Shell Sort Implementation in JavaScript

Main goal: The code sorts an array in ascending order using the Shell sort algorithm by progressively reducing the gap and performing gapped insertion sorts.

Summary description:
A function shellSort(arr) that sorts the input array in place by initially using a gap of half the array length and repeatedly performing insertion sort on elements that are gap apart, shrinking the gap by half each iteration until it becomes 0, and then returning the sorted array.

mbpp_0922.reference_description: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Goal of the maxProduct function

Summary_description:
This function finds two distinct elements in an array whose product is the largest, returning them as an array [x, y]. If the input array has fewer than two elements, it returns null. It does this by checking all pairs (i, j) and keeping track of the pair with the maximum product.

mbpp_0721.reference_description: Write a function to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths for the given square matrix of size n*n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths for the given square matrix of size n*n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Maximize path sum in a grid and compute average value along a specific path

Summary_description:
This code computes the maximum sum obtainable along a path from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner of an N x N grid, where at each step you can move either right or down. It builds a dynamic programming table (dp) where dp[i][j] stores the maximum sum to reach cell (i, j) by adding the corresponding cost[i][j]. The first row and first column are initialized cumulatively. For each internal cell, it takes the maximum of the cell above or to the left, then adds cost[i][j]. Finally, it returns the value at dp[N-1][N-1] divided by (2*N - 1), which seems intended to compute an average along a path of length (2N - 1) (the number of cells in a path from (0,0) to (N-1,N-1) with only right/down moves).

mbpp_0576.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether an array is subarray of another or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to check whether an array is subarray of another or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Subarray Presence Checker (Subarray Matching)

Main goal: The code determines whether array B (length m) appears as a contiguous subarray within array A (length n). It traverses A, attempting to match B sequentially; if a mismatch occurs, it rewinds A's index to the position after the start of the current attempted match and resets the match progress. If a full match of B is found, it returns true; otherwise, after examining A, it returns false.

mbpp_0769.reference_description: Write a javascript function to get the difference between two arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to get the difference between two arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Function to compute symmetric difference between two arrays

Main goal: The diff(li1, li2) function computes the symmetric difference between two arrays. It converts both inputs to sets and returns a new array containing elements that appear in exactly one of the two sets (i.e., elements that are in li1 or li2 but not in both). It preserves no guaranteed order beyond the iteration order of the sets.

mbpp_0034.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the missing number in a sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the missing number in a sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
Goal: The code searches for a missing number in a sorted array of the first N positive integers (1..N) where exactly one number is missing.

What it does:
- Uses a binary search to locate the missing value.
- At each iteration, computes mid and checks:
  - If ar[mid] ≠ mid+1 and ar[mid-1] == mid, then the missing number is mid+1.
  - If ar[mid] ≠ mid+1, search left half (r = mid-1).
  - Otherwise (ar[mid] == mid+1), search right half (l = mid+1).
- Returns the missing number when found, or -1 if not found.

Note: Assumes 0-based indexing with expected value ar[i] = i+1 for a complete sequence.

mbpp_0130.reference_description: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Max Occurrences Finder

Main goal: The code computes the most frequent value in an array and its frequency.

Summary:
- It builds a frequency map (counts) by iterating nums and tallying occurrences for each number.
- It then scans the map to identify the item with the highest count (maxItem) and its count (maxCount).
- It returns a two-element array [maxItem, maxCount], representing the most frequent value and how many times it occurs.

mbpp_0377.reference_description: Write a javascript function to remove all occurrences of a character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to remove all occurrences of a character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
### Summary_description
The code defines removeChar(s, c), which counts how many times character c appears in string s, then removes that many occurrences of c from s (one by one) and returns the resulting string. It builds an array of characters, repeatedly finds and splices out the first occurrence of c until all counted instances are removed, then joins back into a string.

mbpp_0898.reference_description: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element Extraction Based on Consecutive Duplicates

Main goal: The code scans an array of numbers and collects elements that appear in exactly n consecutive duplicates, returning a new array of those elements (one instance per group). It groups consecutive equal numbers, and for each group, if the group's length equals n, it pushes that value into the result.

mbpp_0937.reference_description: Write a function to count the most common character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the most common character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Function to Find the Most Frequent Character

Main goal: Determine and return the character that appears most frequently in a given string. It builds a frequency map for each character, then scans the map to find the character with the highest count. If multiple characters tie, it returns the first one encountered in the counts iteration.

mbpp_0304.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Function to Find Element Considering Rotations and Ranges

Main goal: Determine and return an element from array arr after applying a series of range-based rotations to a given index.

Summary_description:
- The function find_Element takes an array (arr), a 2D array of ranges (ranges), the number of rotation steps (rotations), and an initial index.
- It iterates from the last rotation down to the first. For each rotation, it checks if the current index lies within the corresponding range [left, right].
- If the index is within the range:
  - If the index equals the left bound, the index is moved to the right bound (wrapping to the end of the range).
  - Otherwise, the index is decremented by 1 (moving left within the range).
- After processing all rotations, it returns arr[index], the element at the final computed index.

mbpp_0207.reference_description: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Repeating Subsequence Length Calculator

Main goal: This code computes the length of the longest repeating subsequence in a given string using dynamic programming. It builds a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] stores the length of the longest repeating subsequence within the first i characters and first j characters, counting matches of identical characters at different indices (i != j). The result returned is dp[n][n], the maximum length of a repeating subsequence.

mbpp_0029.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the element occurring odd number of times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the element occurring odd number of times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Get the first odd-occurring element in an array

Main goal of the code:
- The function getOddOccurrence(arr, arrSize) searches for the first element in the array that occurs an odd number of times. It uses a nested loop to count how many times each element appears in the array and returns the first element whose count is odd. If no such element exists, it returns -1.

Key behavior:
- For each i from 0 to arrSize-1, it counts occurrences of arr[i] in the entire array.
- If the count is odd, it immediately returns that element.
- If no element has an odd occurrence, it returns -1.

Notes:
- Time complexity is O(n^2) due to the nested loops.
- It does not handle arrays with non-numeric elements differently; it uses strict equality to compare elements.

mbpp_0438.reference_description: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bidirectional Pair Matcher

Main goal of the code:
- The function countBidirectional(testList) counts the number of unordered pairs of two-element arrays within testList that form a bidirectional relationship. Specifically, it looks for pairs [a, b] and [b, a] appearing at different indices, increments a counter for each such pair, and returns the count as a string.

mbpp_0620.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic programming solution to the largest divisible subset problem

Main goal: Given an array a of length n, the function largestSubset computes the size of the largest subset where for any pair of elements in the subset, one element divides the other (i.e., a subset with pairwise divisibility). It uses a bottom-up DP approach to find the longest chain of numbers where each pair satisfies divisibility in either direction, and returns the maximum chain length.

mbpp_0781.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether the count of divisors is even or odd.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to check whether the count of divisors is even or odd.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Odd or Even Number of Divisors Checker

Main goal of the code:
- Determines whether a given positive integer n has an even or odd number of positive divisors, and returns the string "Even" or "Odd" accordingly.

What the code does:
- Initializes a counter to track the number of divisors of n.
- Iterates i from 1 up to floor(sqrt(n)) + 1 (via limit = Math.floor(Math.sqrt(n)) + 2 and i < limit).
- For each i, checks if i divides n.
  - If i^2 equals n, it counts only one divisor (the square root).
  - Otherwise, it counts two divisors (i and n/i).
- After the loop, returns "Even" if the divisor count is even, or "Odd" if the count is odd.

Notes:
- The function relies on the fact that a number with a perfect square as a divisor pairing has a potential odd total only when n is a perfect square, but the loop optimizes by counting pairs up to sqrt(n).
- The function ultimately reports the parity (even/odd) of the total number of positive divisors of n.

mbpp_0661.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum that can be formed which has no three consecutive elements present.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum that can be formed which has no three consecutive elements present.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Goal and Function of maxSumOfThreeConsecutive

Summary_description:
Computes the maximum sum obtainable by selecting three consecutive elements in an array, using dynamic programming. It builds a dp array where dp[i] represents the maximum sum achievable considering elements up to index i, ensuring the last considered segment ends at or before i. The function initializes base cases for the first three elements and then iteratively updates dp[i] by choosing among: skipping current, including the current with its predecessor, or including the current trio with appropriate previous best. It finally returns the best sum for the entire array (dp[n - 1]).

mbpp_0842.reference_description: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Odd Occurrence Finder in an Array

Main goal of the code:
- The function getOddOccurrence scans an array to find and return the first element that occurs an odd number of times. It counts how many times each array element appears in the entire array and returns the first element whose count is odd. If no such element exists, it returns -1.

Key behavior:
- For each element arr[i], it tallies its total occurrences by comparing with every element arr[j].
- If a value has an odd count, it is immediately returned as the result.
- If no value has an odd count, the function returns -1.

mbpp_0498.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find gcd of two positive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find gcd of two positive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: GCD Computation by Trial Division

Main goal: The code computes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers x and y by checking divisors starting from floor(y/2) down to 1, with an early fast-path if y divides x.

Summary description:
- Function gcd(x, y) initializes gcd to 1.
- If x is divisible by y, it returns y immediately (a quick path for y as a divisor of x).
- Otherwise, it iterates k from floor(y/2) down to 1, and for the first k that divides both x and y, it sets gcd to k and breaks.
- Finally, it returns gcd (either the found common divisor or 1 if none found).

mbpp_0510.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming Subsequence Count Based on Divisibility and Threshold

Main goal of the code: Compute a count of subsequences of the input array that meet a specific condition involving the subsequence elements and a target k, using a dynamic programming table. The function builds a 2D DP array where dp[i][j] represents the number of valid subsequences considering the first j elements of the array with respect to the threshold i. It iterates over i from 1 to k and over j from 1 to n, updating counts by either skipping the current element or including it when the current element is positive and ≤ i, adding counts tied to the quotient floor(i / arr[j-1]) from the previous column, plus one. Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dutch National Flag Sorting Algorithm Implementation

Main goal of the code:
- Sort an array consisting of only 0s, 1s, and 2s in-place so that all 0s come first, followed by all 1s, then all 2s. It uses the Dutch National Flag algorithm (three-pointer partitioning) to partition the array in a single pass.

Summary of how it works:
- low tracks the boundary for 0s, mid traverses the array, and high tracks the boundary for 2s.
- If arr[mid] is 0: swap with arr[low], increment both low and mid.
- If arr[mid] is 1: simply move mid forward.
- If arr[mid] is 2: swap with arr[high], decrement high, without advancing mid (to recheck the swapped value).
- Repeats until mid passes high; returns the sorted array in-place.

mbpp_0571.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum possible sum of disjoint pairs for the given array of integers and a number k.

Title: Maximum Sum of Non-Overlapping Pairs with Difference Constraint

Main goal: This code finds the maximum possible sum by selecting disjoint pairs of elements from the array such that the difference between the two elements in a chosen pair is less than K. Pairs are formed from sorted adjacent elements, and each element can belong to at most one pair. The function returns the maximum achievable sum of the selected pairs.

What it does:
- Sorts the array in non-decreasing order.

- Returns dp[N-1], the maximum sum achievable with the entire array.

mbpp_0923.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Short Summary of What the Code Does

Main goal of the code: It computes the length of the shortest common supersequence (SCS) for two strings X and Y using a recursive approach.

Key behavior:
- If one string is exhausted (m == 0 or n == 0), returns the length of the other remaining string.
- If the last characters of the current prefixes match, it recurses on the remaining prefixes (m-1, n-1) and adds 1.
- If the last characters differ, it recurses on two possibilities (deleting one char from either X or Y) and takes the minimum of those plus 1, effectively counting the length of the SCS.

Note: m and n represent the lengths considered from X and Y, respectively. The function is a direct recursive computation without memoization, so it may be inefficient for longer inputs.

mbpp_0113.reference_description: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Integer String Validator

Main goal: The code defines checkInteger(text) which trims input and returns true if the string represents a non-negative integer (digits only) or a signed integer with an optional leading + or -; returns null for empty input and false for non-matching strings.

mbpp_0286.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Subarray Sum over K Repetitions

Main goal: Compute the maximum subarray sum for an array a of length n, but allowing up to k concatenations (i.e., considering a repeated sequence a repeated k times). The function iterates through n*k elements in a circular fashion, using Kadane-like logic to track the best subarray sum across the repeated sequence, returning the overall maximum sum found.

mbpp_0134.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Summary of the checkLast function

Main goal: The function computes the sum of the first n elements of an array and, if p equals 1, returns "ODD" when the sum is even and "EVEN" when the sum is odd; for any other value of p, it always returns "EVEN".

mbpp_0275.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the position of the last removed element from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the position of the last removed element from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Summary of getPosition Function

Main goal of the code:
- The function processes an array a of length n, dividing each element by m with ceiling, then scans from the end to find the last position where the value is strictly greater than all previously seen values (i.e., the last index of the new maximum in the reversed pass). It returns that 1-based index; if no change occurs, it returns 1 (since result starts at -1 and is updated when a[i] > maxx, finally returning result + 1).

What it does:
- For i from 0 to n-1: a[i] = ceil(a[i] / m).
- Then iterates i from n-1 down to 0, tracking the maximum value encountered (maxx). Whenever a[i] > maxx, updates maxx and records result = i.
- Returns result + 1 (converting to 1-based index).

mbpp_0311.reference_description: Write a javascript function to set the left most unset bit.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to set the left most unset bit.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Set Leftmost Unset Bit in Integer

Main goal of the code:
- The function setLeftMostUnsetBit(n) finds the leftmost (most significant) 0 bit in the binary representation of n and returns a new number with that bit set to 1, leaving all other bits unchanged. If n already has all lower bits set such that n & (n+1) == 0, it returns n as is.

What it does:
- Checks if n already has no unset bit (i.e., n & (n + 1) == 0). If true, returns n.
- Otherwise, iterates through the bits from least significant to most significant to locate the most significant 0 bit (the last 0 encountered when scanning from LSB to MSB). It tracks its position as pos.
- Sets that bit using n | (1 << pos) and returns the resulting number.

Notes:
- The loop identifies the highest-position 0 bit among the bits present in n (within its current length). If there are trailing upper bits beyond the most significant 1, they are not considered since the loop stops when temp becomes 0.

mbpp_0828.reference_description: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Function to count letters, digits, and special characters in a string

Summary_description:
It defines countAlphaDigSpl that iterates over a string and counts how many characters are alphabets (A–Z, a–z), how many are digits (0–9), and how many are any other characters (special). It returns an array [alphabets, digits, special].

mbpp_0657.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Digit of Factorial (Nonzero, Leading Digit)

Main goal: The code computes the leading (most significant) nonzero digit of n!, by iteratively calculating the factorial while removing trailing zeros and keeping the number manageable, then extracting the single leading digit. It multiplies 1..n, strips trailing zeros after each multiplication, truncates to an integer, and finally reduces the result to its most significant digit.

mbpp_0575.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count-Until-Nth Non-Multiple Finder

Main goal: The function countNo(A, N, L, R) searches the inclusive range [L, R] to find the N-th number that is not a multiple of A, returning that value (or undefined if fewer than N non-multiples exist in the range). It iterates from L to R, increments a counter whenever i % A !== 0, and stops when the counter reaches N, returning the current i as result.

mbpp_0355.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count of Integer Pairs Inside a Circle

Main goal: The function count_Rectangles(radius) counts the number of integer coordinate pairs (a, b) with 1 ≤ a < 2*radius and 1 ≤ b < 2*radius whose squared distance a^2 + b^2 is less than or equal to (2*radius)^2, effectively counting lattice points (in the first quadrant, excluding axes) inside or on a circle of radius 2*radius centered at the origin.

mbpp_0110.reference_description: Write a function to extract the ranges that are missing from the given array with the given start range and end range values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract the ranges that are missing from the given array with the given start range and end range values.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: extractMissing — Build Missing Ranges Between Subranges

Main goal: Given a list of subranges (testList) and a start and stop value, the function constructs a sequence of missing or uncovered ranges between the start and stop values by iterating through the subranges and, whenever the current position is beyond the next subrange start, it records a missing segment from startVal to that start. It then advances startVal to the end of the subrange and continues, finally returning an array of [missingStart, missingEnd] intervals that represent gaps within [startVal, stopVal] relative to the provided subranges.

mbpp_0225.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary Search-Based Finding of Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array with Duplicates

Main goal of the code:
- The function findMin(arr, low, high) returns the minimum element in a rotated sorted array (which may contain duplicates) within the index range [low, high]. It uses a modified binary search to narrow the search space by comparing the middle element to the high element, handling duplicates by reducing the high pointer when arr[mid] equals arr[high], and adjusting low/high accordingly to converge on the minimum value.

mbpp_0047.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Purpose and behavior of computeLastDigit function

Main goal: Compute the last digit of the product of consecutive integers from A+1 up to B (i.e., the product of numbers in the range (A, B]), with some early-exit optimizations.

What it does:
- If A equals B, returns 1 (empty product convention).
- If the range size B - A is at least 5, returns 0 (the product contains at least one multiple of 10 or enough factors to yield a trailing zero, making the last digit 0).
- Otherwise, iteratively multiplies the last digits of each integer in (A, B], keeping only the last digit at each step (variable = (variable * (i % 10)) % 10) and finally returns the resulting last digit.

mbpp_0140.reference_description: Write a function to extract elements that occur singly in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract elements that occur singly in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Extract Unique Elements Preserving First-Occurrence Order

Main goal of the code: It flattens a list of iterables and returns a new array containing each distinct element exactly once, preserving the order in which elements first appear across all inner iterables.

mbpp_0487.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of tuples in increasing order by the last element in each tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of tuples in increasing order by the last element in each tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bubble-sort by Last Element of Subarrays

Summary_description: The code defines sortTuple(tup), which bubble-sorts an array of subarrays (tup) in ascending order based on the last element of each subarray. It repeatedly compares tup[j].last and tup[j+1].last, swapping entire subarrays when the former is larger, and returns the sorted array.

mbpp_0384.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description: 
The code defines a function frequencyOfSmallest(n, arr) that finds the smallest value in the array and returns how many times that smallest value occurs. It initializes with the first element as the current minimum and a frequency of 1, then scans the array to update the minimum and reset the count when a new smaller value is found, or increment the count when an equal minimum is encountered. The function ultimately returns the frequency of the smallest element.

mbpp_0489.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of the Largest Value (as implemented in the code)

Main goal of the code:
- The function frequency_Of_Largest(n, arr) is intended to compute how many times the current maximum value appears in the array. However, due to a logic error, it instead tracks the frequency of the smallest value found so far while iterating, effectively returning the count of occurrences of the smallest element encountered after the first element. The function initializes mn to arr[0] and freq to 1, updates mn when it finds a larger value (resetting the count to 1), and increments freq when an element equals the current mn. The end result is the frequency of the smallest value witnessed that is less than or equal to all previously seen values, not the largest value.

mbpp_0255.reference_description: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: The code generates all n-length combinations of elements from an input array, allowing repeated elements and preserving non-decreasing index order (i.e., combinations with replacement). The function combinationsWithReplacement recursively builds all tails and prefixes to produce arrays of length n. The helper combinationsColors(l, n) simply delegates to this same behavior.

mbpp_0546.reference_description: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Purpose and behavior of last_occurence_char function

Main goal: To find the position of the last occurrence of a given character in a string and return a 1-based index, or null if the character does not occur.

What it does:
- Iterates through the string from start to end.
- Tracks the index (flag) of every match; after the loop, flag holds the index of the last match (0-based).
- If the character never occurs, returns null.
- If it occurs at least once, returns flag + 1 (i.e., the 1-based position of the last occurrence).

mbpp_0505.reference_description: Write a function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

The function iterates through A, compacting truthy values toward the start and recording the count k, then fills the rest of the array with 0s. It returns the modified array.

mbpp_0559.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: The function maxSubArraySum computes and returns the largest sum of any contiguous subarray within the given array a of length size, using a variation of Kadane's algorithm that resets the running sum to zero when it becomes negative and tracks the maximum sum seen.

mbpp_0589.reference_description: Write a function to find perfect squares between two given numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find perfect squares between two given numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find Perfect Squares in a Range

Main goal: The function perfectSquares(a, b) scans all integers from a to b inclusive and collects those numbers that are perfect squares (i.e., equal to j*j for some integer j). It returns an array of all perfect squares within the given range.

mbpp_0627.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: findFirstMissing - Binary Search for First Missing Non-Negative Integer

Main goal: Given an array where indices are expected to match values (i.e., array[i] should equal i for a perfect sequence of non-negative integers), the function findFirstMissing(array, start, end) returns the smallest non-negative integer that is missing from the array within the range [start, end]. It uses a binary-search-like approach:
- If start > end, returns end + 1 as the first missing.
- If array[start] != start, the first missing is at index start.
- It computes mid and recursively searches left or right half depending on whether array[mid] equals mid, effectively locating the first index where array[i] != i.

mbpp_0681.reference_description: Write a javascript function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
### Title: Smallest Divisor Finder

### Main goal
This function computes and returns the smallest positive divisor of a given integer n. If n is even, it immediately returns 2. Otherwise, it tests odd numbers starting from 3 up to sqrt(n); if it finds a divisor, it returns it. If no divisors are found, it returns n, indicating that n is prime (or 1).

mbpp_0650.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a javascript function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Equality Checker for Two Arrays After Sorting

Main goal of the code:
- Determine whether two input arrays contain the same elements with the same multiplicities, regardless of order.

What the functions do:
- areEqual(arr1, arr2, n, m) takes two arrays and their lengths.
- It first checks if lengths n and m are equal; if not, returns false.
- It sorts both arrays in ascending order.
- It compares elements pairwise up to index n-2 (note: an off-by-one issue). If any corresponding elements differ, returns false.
- If all compared elements are equal, returns true.

Important note: There is a bug in the loop (it should iterate to i < n, not i < n - 1) which causes it to skip the last elements during comparison.

mbpp_0605.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Prime Number Check Function

Main goal: The code defines a function prime_num(num) intended to determine whether a given number num is prime, returning true if prime and false otherwise. However, due to a logic error inside the loop, it misclassifies many numbers.

Summary description:
- If num < 1, returns false.
- For num >= 1, it loops i from 2 up to floor(num/2) - 1, and for the first i it checks divisibility:
  - If num % i === 0, returns false (not prime).
  - Otherwise, immediately returns true (claims prime) after checking just the first divisor, which is incorrect for most numbers. The loop does not continue to test all potential divisors.

mbpp_0903.reference_description: Write a javascript function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.

main goal: The code counts how many even bits (0 bits) appear in the binary representations of all integers from 1 to n by iterating each number, examining its bits, and incrementing the counter whenever a bit is 0.

mbpp_0829.reference_description: Write a function to find out the second most repeated (or frequent) string in the given sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the second most repeated (or frequent) string in the given sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Find the element that has the second highest frequency (second most frequent) in the given array and return that element.

What it does:
- Builds a frequency map (counts) of each item in the array.
- Collects all frequency values, sorts them in descending order, and selects the second largest frequency.
- Iterates the frequency map to find the first key whose count equals the second largest frequency and returns that key.

Notes:
- If there are ties for the second highest frequency, it returns the first key (in enumeration order) matching that count.
- If the array has fewer than two distinct values, behavior may be undefined (no explicit handling for edge cases).

mbpp_0745.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.

mbpp_0874.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check if the string is a concatenation of another string.

mbpp_0147.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.

mbpp_0125.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum difference between the number of 0s and number of 1s in any sub-string of the given binary string.

Summary_description: The code scans a binary string of length n, treating '0' as +1 and '1' as -1, and uses a Kadane-style algorithm to compute the maximum subarray sum. mbpp_0952.reference_description: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Efficiently Computes nCr Mod p

Main goal of the code:
- This function calculates the binomial coefficient C(n, r) modulo p (i.e., n choose r modulo p) without using factorials or modular inverses.
- It uses a dynamic programming approach to build up the binomial coefficients row by row, storing only up to r+1 values to save space.
- It optimizes by using r = min(r, n - r) to reduce the number of iterations and ensure the inner loop runs fewer times.
- The final result returned is C(n, r) mod p.

mbpp_0974.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Min-sum path in a triangle using dynamic programming

Summary_description:
The code computes the minimum-sum path from the top to the bottom of a triangle-like 2D array A. It initializes a memo array with the last row, then iterates upward from the second-to-last row, updating memo[j] to A[i][j] plus the minimum of the two possible downward moves (memo[j] and memo[j+1]). At the end, memo[0] contains the minimum total sum along a path from the top to the bottom.

mbpp_0187.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) Recursive Function

Main goal of the code:
- Computes the length of the longest common subsequence between two arrays/strings X and Y using a simple recursive approach.

What the functions do:
- longestCommonSubsequence(X, Y, m, n) takes two sequences X and Y and their current lengths m and n.
- Base case: if either m or n is 0, returns 0 (no common subsequence).
- If the last elements match (X[m-1] === Y[n-1]), it counts this match and recurses on the prefixes (m-1, n-1), adding 1.
- If the last elements do not match, it recursively computes the LCS length by excluding one element at a time from either X or Y, and returns the maximum of those two possibilities (m, n-1) and (m-1, n).

Notes:
- This is a straightforward but inefficient exponential-time implementation due to overlapping subproblems (no memoization).

mbpp_0706.reference_description: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.

- Iterates through the first n elements of arr2 and checks whether each element exists in the hash set.

Summary:
- isSubset(arr1, m, arr2, n) returns true if arr2[0..n-1] is a subset of arr1[0..m-1], otherwise false. It uses a hash set for O(1) average membership checks.

mbpp_0385.reference_description: Write a function to find the n'th perrin number using recursion.

mbpp_0414.reference_description: Write a javascript function to check whether the value exists in a sequence or not.

mbpp_0943.reference_description: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.

mbpp_0757.reference_description: Write a function to count the pairs of reverse strings in the given string array.

mbpp_0961.reference_description: Write a function to convert a roman numeral to an integer.

mbpp_0867.reference_description: Write a javascript function to add a minimum number such that the sum of array becomes even.

mbpp_0092.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given number is undulating or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given number is undulating or not.

What the code does:

Overall, it recursively computes Eulerian numbers A(n, m) via the well-known recurrence.

Title: Digit Sum Decomposition into Two Parts

Main goal of the code:
- Compute the sum of digits of a number N by splitting N into two parts: a largest number consisting of all 9s not exceeding N, and the remaining prefix, then summing the digit sums of those two parts.

Functions:
- sumDigitsSingle(x): Returns the sum of the decimal digits of x by repeatedly taking the last digit (x % 10) and truncating the last digit (Math.floor(x / 10)).
- closest(x): Builds the largest number composed of 9s that is less than or equal to x. It starts with 0 and appends 9s by iteratively setting ans = ans * 10 + 9 until the next append would exceed x.
- sumDigitsTwoParts(N): Finds A = closest(N) (the largest 9…9 number ≤ N), then returns sumDigitsSingle(A) plus sumDigitsSingle(N - A). This effectively computes the sum of digits of N by separating it into A and the remainder.
